facility_roles.quote: NA38 is a dedicated experiment for the study of muon pairs produced in interactions of ultra-relativistic ions with dense matter.

facility_roles.note: Proton, oxygen and sulphur beams from the SPS (accelerator:sps); H10 beam line per Greybook.
facility_roles.quote: At first, the pioneering experiment NA38 [113] collected data with light ions (oxygen and sulphur) at 200 GeV/nucleon and with proton beams at 450 GeV, using the NA10 dimuon spectrometer and an electromagnetic calorimeter as a centrality detector.

intervals.label: data taking (proton, oxygen and sulphur beams)
intervals.note: The start is stated (data taken from the fall of 1986: first 200 GeV protons on uranium, then oxygen ions; the 1988 NA38 paper). intervals.quote: It had started its data taking with oxygen beams in 1986

intervals.label: completed
intervals.note: Terminal event inferred from the last documented NA38 data set (S+U, 1992); no fetched source states the NA38 end date. NA50 followed with Pb beams (first documented Pb-Pb sample 1995).

name: NA38
notes: Hall not identified: placed at the generic Prévessin North Area site (Greybook gives the beam line, H10, but no fetched source names the hall).
NA38 reused the NA10 muon spectrometer (arXiv:2603.10835: 'built as a modest upgrade of the older NA10 experiment'); NA10 is not an Atlas record.
NA50 followed NA38 (Specht 2014 slides, Tserruya 1998, arXiv:hep-ph/0412158); the lineage row (predecessor) is on experiment:na50.
Spokesperson Louis Kluberg and contact person Peter Sonderegger (NA38 website, Greybook). No formation date or membership found.

physics_goals.locator: NA38 paper, Z. Phys. C 38 (1988) 117, Introduction (J/psi suppression: arXiv:2603.10835, Section 1)
physics_goals.quote: NA38 is a dedicated experiment for the study of muon pairs produced in interactions of ultra-relativistic ions with dense matter.
physics_goals.value: Study muon pairs produced in interactions of ultra-relativistic ions with dense matter, including J/psi production and its suppression as a signature of quark-gluon plasma formation

summary.plain: NA38 was a CERN experiment that counted pairs of muons produced when oxygen and sulphur ions hit uranium and other targets. It reported that J/psi particles were made less often in the most violent collisions, an early sign later linked to quark-gluon plasma.
summary.technical: NA38: NA10 air-core toroidal dimuon spectrometer (multiwire chambers, scintillator hodoscopes) with a scintillating-fibre electromagnetic calorimeter for transverse energy, a multiple active uranium target and beam hodoscopes, on the H10 beam line of the SPS North Area; p (200 and 450 GeV), O and S (200A GeV) beams, 1986-1992; J/psi yield versus transverse energy in O-U; precursor of NA50.

unique_capabilities.quote: The apparatus consists of a muon spectrometer, an electromagnetic calorimeter, a multiple active target and specific beam detectors
unique_capabilities.value: NA10 air-core toroidal dimuon spectrometer with an electromagnetic calorimeter, a multiple active uranium target and beam detectors, run at very high beam intensities
